entities.summary: Edward Granville Eliot, 3rd Earl of St Germans, styled Lord Elliot from 1823–45, was a British politician, peer, and diplomat. Born into the prominent Eliot family, he was educated at Christ Church, Oxford, before entering politics. He served as a Member of Parliament for the borough of St Germans, and later as a diplomat in France and Italy. His career was marked by controversy and scandal, including a high-profile duel and accusations of corruption. Despite his questionable legacy, Eliot's tenure as Earl of St Germans reflects the complex and often tumultuous nature of British politics during the early 19th century. In the years following his death, his family's influence continued to shape British society, with his great-nephew, Lord Herbert Eliot, going on to become a prominent figure in British politics.
